cards.subject: Zin-Azshari
lines: This ground was part of the night elf capital before the Sundering tore it apart, and the zone carries the name of the queen who was driven mad and lost it.
A high-level zone with almost nothing in it, sitting on the address of the greatest city the world ever had.

cards.subject: The emptiest zone in the game
lines: "One of, if not the most unpopulated zone in the game player-wise."
It blames the quest count — "some of which are parts of uncompleted chains" — and the fact that you cannot easily get between the beaches and the tops of the cliffs.
Most players finish this game without ever entering it.

cards.subject: Eternal autumn
lines: "A beautiful coastal area cloaked in eternal autumn. The trees and other flora are tinged in brilliant oranges and reds, and nearer the coast, great cliffs and sandy beaches line the ocean."
It is the best-looking empty room in the game.

cards.subject: Eldarath fell into the sea
lines: A flourishing night elf city, a mighty stronghold, before the Sundering. Most of it collapsed into the Bay of Storms below.
What you walk through on the eastern cliffs is the part that did not fall.
The rest is under the water you are looking at.

cards.subject: Temple of Zin-Malor
lines: A night elven place of worship dedicated to Elune, built in the same family of shapes as the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus.
A naga warlord lives in it now.
Stand in a Darnassus you cannot enter.

cards.subject: The Ravencrest Monument
lines: An ancient night elven colossus on the southern cliffs, broken off at the knees with the pieces scattered around it.
Everyone assumes it honours Lord Kur'talos Ravencrest. There is not enough left to confirm that, and what survives appears to be a woman.
You can only reach it inland. There is no way up from the sea.

cards.subject: The battleground that never opened
lines: Azshara Crater was to be the game's fourth battleground, forty on forty, on the scale of Alterac Valley.
The terrain was built and left in the files. It was still being talked about years later and never opened.
Both sides' fortifications are cut into the ridge. The approach roads are there to walk.

cards.subject: Azuregos
cards.tag: One of the first two world bosses
lines: Added alongside Lord Kazzak in patch 1.3.0. A blue dragon trusted by Malygos with the safekeeping of his flight's most precious things.
He is here because Eldarath is here.
He is guarding a ruined city and whatever the night elves left in it.

cards.subject: It is in a fish
lines: Malygos gave Azuregos a shard of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands to protect.
He hid it inside a minnow.
To get it back you build an arcanite buoy to lure the fish out. A piece of a legendary artefact, in a fish, as a joke.

cards.subject: There are two of him
lines: During the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj event Blizzard added a second, unkillable Azuregos.
Raids were killing the real one faster than questers could talk to him.
One of the two dragons in this zone is a workaround.

cards.subject: Grinding magic into dust
lines: Elves in the north dig for Highborne artefacts and pulverise what they find into Glittering Dust.
They also carry a Kaldorei Tome of Summoning.
Magus Rimtori made a deal with the Horde over the expedition's profits and broke it.

cards.subject: The Timbermaw are here too
lines: The southeastern mountains hold furbolg villages — outposts of Timbermaw Hold and Ursolan, both Azshara subzones.
On the cliff above them stands Xylem's Tower, with an archmage and his high elf apprentices in it.
Nothing sends you to either.

cards.subject: Under the Bay of Storms
lines: There is a flooded temple down there, and a sea giant who asks mortals to help him kill a hydra queen.
A giant, a many-headed queen and a drowned shrine.
In the corner of the map nobody visits.
